info.title: classifier.dev
info.summary: Zero-shot text classification with calibrated confidence. Free without a key; Pro for 10x limits.
info.description:
Send text and a list of labels, receive the label that fits, a calibrated confidence and a score per label. Up to 1,000 texts per request, ~1s. Tiers: fast (default) and smart, which re-asks answers below 0.7 confidence of a fast reasoning model. Free limits are per IP and counted in classifications: 3,000/min and 20,000/day on fast, 200/min and 2,000/day on smart. Benchmarks: https://classifier.dev/benchmark

Authentication: optional for classification. Pro ($20/month) bearer keys provide fast 30,000/min and 200,000/day, smart 2,000/min and 20,000/day per billing account across IPs. Partner keys remain supported (see https://classifier.dev/auth.md).

Versioning: the current major is v1, addressed as POST /v1/classify; POST / is an alias that tracks the current major. Response shapes are additive within a major (fields are added, never renamed or removed). Every response carries an x-api-version header. A breaking change ships as /v2 beside /v1, and /v1 then carries Deprecation and Sunset headers (RFC 9745 / RFC 8594) for at least six months before removal.

Rate limits: RateLimit-Limit and RateLimit-Policy (IETF draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers) on every classification response, RateLimit-Remaining once the limiter has been consulted (every 200 and 429), Retry-After on 429s. Idempotency: classification has no side effects; an Idempotency-Key header is accepted and echoed so generic retry logic keeps working.

Errors: every non-2xx body is {error, code} — see components.schemas.Error for the codes. The two GET forms answer plain text (`error:`, `usage:`, `try:` lines) unless ?verbose=1 or Accept: application/json asks for the JSON object.

MCP: the same capability as tools at https://classifier.dev/mcp (Streamable HTTP, no auth), documented at https://classifier.dev/mcp-setup. Batch: the inputs array is the batch operation — up to 1,000 texts per request; POST /v1/classify/batch is an alias for callers that look for one.

x-api-versioning.deprecationSignal: Deprecation and Sunset response headers, at least 180 days notice

post.summary: Subscribe a human or agent inbox to product updates
post.description: Use your own email address, or one whose owner explicitly requested updates. No API key or browser is required. Check the inbox and POST the emailed token to /subscribe/confirm before updates start. Tokens expire within 24 hours; repeated requests within the same clock hour send at most one email. Addresses are trimmed and lowercased. Signup does not add an active subscriber. Existing unsubscribes are preserved. One email when a roadmap item ships; reply to unsubscribe. Limited to 5 requests/minute and 50/day per IP.

email.description: An email address for an inbox you control or have explicit permission to subscribe.

wants.description: Optional. The roadmap items the subscriber would use first: private (private inference), dedicated (dedicated endpoints), trained (trained endpoints), api (a self-serve api), accuracy (better classification). Unknown keys are ignored. The list rides in the confirmation token and is stored on confirmation; a later confirmation that names some replaces the earlier choice, one that names none keeps it.

202.description: Confirmation email accepted by the mail provider. The address is not yet subscribed.

wants.description: The roadmap keys that were accepted, in roadmap order.

429.description: Too many signups; wait Retry-After seconds before retrying.

post.summary: Confirm mailbox ownership using the emailed token
post.description: Submit the token from the confirmation email. Invalid or expired tokens cannot subscribe an address. Repeated confirmation is safe and never undoes an unsubscribe. GET renders a confirmation form without changing subscription state.

200.description: Mailbox confirmed; existing unsubscribe preferences remain in effect.

wants.description: The roadmap keys recorded with the confirmation.

400.description: Invalid or expired token. Subscribe again for a fresh email.

503.description: Confirmation storage unavailable. Retry the same token shortly.

post.summary: Submit a SKILL.md for review; listed if it passes
post.description: Send the text of a SKILL.md (YAML front matter with name and description, then Markdown; 200 to 24,000 characters). It is reviewed in three passes, each a gate: a static scanner blocks instruction overrides, hidden text, credential reads, exfiltration, remote code execution, destructive and persistent commands, secrets and obfuscation; the decision model (Jev) scores intent, genuineness, usefulness and spam as calibrated probabilities; a reasoning model then scores safety, usefulness, novelty and clarity out of 10 with reasons. The answer is the review either way: 201 with the listing when accepted, 200 with {accepted: false, stage, reasons} when not, and nothing is stored on a rejection. Do not put instructions to the reviewer in the skill; they are treated as evidence of manipulation. 5 reviews an hour per IP, 200 a day for everyone.

skill.description: The SKILL.md text, front matter included.

author.description: Shown beside the listing: a handle, a name or a URL. Optional.

source.description: An https link to where the skill lives. Optional.

200.description: Reviewed and not listed. `stage` says which pass refused it and `reasons` say why.

400.description: The body is not {skill: string}, the text is too long, or `source` is not an https URL. `code` is bad_json or skill_invalid.

409.description: The same skill text is already listed; the body carries its `url`. `code` is duplicate_skill.

429.description: Over the review budget. `code` is rate_limit_hour (this IP) or rate_limit_day (everyone).

503.description: A review model is unavailable; nothing was stored. `code` is review_unavailable; retry after Retry-After.

default.description: Any other error, same {error, code} shape.

post.summary: Agents report a problem or a suggestion (feedback.now protocol). Returns a receipt to poll.
post.description: Asynchronous: the report is accepted immediately and scored, deduplicated and forwarded in the background. The response carries a receipt with an `id` and a `status`; poll GET /api/v1/receipts/{id} until `status` is final. Categories, evidence types and limits are at GET /api/v1/policy and /.well-known/agent-feedback.json. No authentication.

202.description: Accepted for processing. `Location` points at the receipt to poll; the body carries the same id.

Location.description: GET here until status is final.

id.description: Job id; GET /api/v1/receipts/{id} returns its state.

poll.description: URL to poll for the final state.

get.summary: Classify a single text. Returns the bare label as plain text.
get.description: The quickest possible call: labels comma-separated in the first path segment, the text in the rest. Spaces may be written as + or %20. A raw comma, slash or plus is a separator; a label's own comma, slash or plus sign is written percent-encoded (%2C, %2F, %2B), so /C%2B%2B,python/... reads the label C++. Add ?verbose=1 (or send Accept: application/json) for JSON including calibrated confidence and per-label scores. The same request works as query parameters on the root, GET /?labels=spam,not+spam&text=Win+a+free+iPhone, with the same options; a malformed request answers with a URL that would have worked.

parameters.name: labels
parameters.description: Comma-separated categories, 2 to 100.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The text to classify, up to 32,000 characters.

parameters.name: tier
parameters.description: fast or smart, any case. Anything else is a 400 bad_tier rather than a silent fast.

parameters.name: instructions
parameters.description: Extra criteria, e.g. judge the reviewer's overall verdict.

parameters.name: verbose
parameters.description: Set to 1 to receive JSON instead of a bare label. Accept: application/json does the same.

parameters.name: multi
parameters.description: Set to 1 to return every category that applies, one per line (an array under `labels` with ?verbose=1).

parameters.name: max_labels
parameters.description: Cap on how many labels a multi-label answer returns; implies multi. Zero or less means no cap.

200.description: The chosen label, or JSON when verbose=1 or Accept: application/json

FeedbackReport.description: A feedback.now 1.1 report. Only `signal.category` and one of `content.title` or `content.summary` are required; every other field raises the quality score the receipt reports. Vocabularies are the ones GET /api/v1/policy serves.

reporter.description: Who is reporting. Shown on the report as `vendor / product / version`.

surface.description: The endpoint, page or command, e.g. `POST /v1/classify`.

content.description: `title` or `summary` is required. A missing title is taken from the summary.

hypothesis.description: What the reporter thinks is going on.

evidence.description: More can be added later with POST /api/v1/feedback/{id}/attachments.

content.description: Text, or any JSON value, which is stored serialised.

content.title: POST /v1/classify returns 404
content.summary: The documented path answers 404 not_found while POST / classifies the same body.
content.hypothesis: The route was dropped in a recent deploy.

Observation.description: The flat body POST /api/v1/observations reads: a category and one sentence.

example.summary: The 404 body names an endpoint that also 404s.

inputs: postgres index tuning for ML feature stores

dimensions.description: Named dimensions. Each is a label array or {labels, instructions}. At most 1,000 item × dimension decisions; definitions at most 16,000 characters combined.

items.description: Alias for inputs in dimensions mode. Do not combine with input or inputs.

input.description: A single text. Provide this or inputs; a string under `inputs` is read as one text too.

inputs.description: Up to 1,000 texts classified in one call, results in the same order. Public smart requests accept at most 200 so the batch fits its per-minute quota.

labels.description: Semantic category names. 'urgent bug' classifies better than 'p0'.

tier.description: smart re-asks single-label answers below 0.7 confidence of a reasoning model; multi-label ignores it. Read case-insensitively; any other value is a 400 bad_tier.

multi.description: Return every label that applies, with a score per label. true, "true", 1 and "1" all mean yes.

max_labels.description: Cap on how many multi-label answers come back; implies multi. A numeric string is read; zero or less means no cap; a fraction is rounded down.

confidence.description: 0 to 1, calibrated: how likely the chosen label is right among your labels. Measured on six-way emotion, answers >= 0.9 were right 82% of the time and answers < 0.5 were right 29%. It is not a fit score — text matching none of your categories still gets one; add a label such as 'none of these' for that. Null only when withheld; see unscored.

scores.description: Probability per label. Sums to 1 for single-label; independent per label for multi-label.

escalated.description: Present and true on the smart tier when the answer was re-asked of the reasoning model; confidence and scores remain the decision model's.

unscored.description: Present only when confidence and scores were withheld because the input does not read as natural language. Treat the label as unreliable.

labels.description: With ?multi=1 only: every label scoring >= 0.7, most likely first. `label` is then the first of them, or empty, and confidence is null.

confidence.description: Jev's distribution-derived confidence. Null for unreadable inputs or after smart escalation; not a literal probability of correctness.

model.description: The model used for every result, or `mixed` when the batch used more than one model.

modelsUsed.description: Every model that served at least one result, in first-use order.

dimensions.description: Dimensions mode: one field result per supplied dimension, in an input-ordered results array.

labels.description: Multi-label mode only, in place of `label`: every label scoring >= 0.7, most likely first.

items.description: Dimensions mode: number of input items.

dimensions.description: Dimensions mode: number of fields per item.

fallback.description: Dimensions mode: fields served by the LLM fallback because Jev was unavailable.

classifications.description: Decisions made. In dimensions mode, items multiplied by dimensions; each counts toward the quota.

escalated.description: How many answers the smart tier re-asked.

escalation_failed.description: Present only when some smart-tier re-asks could not reach the reasoning model; those results carry the fast answer without `escalated`.

summary.description: Per test set (ag_news, emotion): n, how many items Jev was unsure about, and one row per run (jev, fast, smart).

jev.description: Calibrated probabilities from the decision model.

judge.description: The reasoning model's scores, out of 10, with reasons.

install.description: A shell line that saves it where Claude Code looks for skills.

findings.description: Every scanner finding, blocks and warnings.

error.description: Human-readable message saying what to change.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code: one of the listed values, or typesafe_<status> / openrouter_<status> carrying the upstream HTTP status. 400: bad_dimensions, too_many_decisions, dimension_context_too_large, bad_json, no_input, too_many_inputs, too_few_labels, too_many_labels, empty_label, duplicate_labels, empty_input, input_too_long, bad_tier, bad_cursor, invalid_submission, skill_invalid. 404: not_found. 409: duplicate_skill. 429: rate_limit_minute, rate_limit_day, rate_limit_hour. 502: typesafe, typesafe_<status>, openrouter_<status>, chain_exhausted, batch_unavailable, timeout, upstream_other. 500: internal. 503: review_unavailable.

upgrade.description: On a free-tier 429: the page where a plan lifts this limit (https://classifier.dev/pro). Absent on Pro and partner keys.

usage.description: GET forms only, on a 400: the two URL shapes.

try.description: GET forms only, on a 400: a URL built from what was sent that would have worked.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Optional. Classification has no side effects, so any retry is already safe; the key is accepted and echoed back unchanged so generic retry logic keeps working.

partnerKey.description: Optional for classification. Pro keys (classifier_pro_...) provide 10x limits per billing account; subscribe at https://classifier.dev/pro. Partner keys retain separately arranged access. See https://classifier.dev/auth.md.
